## The two that weren't straight expenses

The key call here was that two of the five don't belong in March P&L:

- **Delmar** is a 12-month D&O premium (3/1/26–2/28/27). Policy 4 requires prepaid treatment; coverage begins in March so I recognized month 1 (800) and left 8,800 on the balance sheet.
- **Meridian** is a booth deposit for a **June** expo. Policy 4 explicitly names "deposits for future events" — it releases to 6400 when the event occurs. Expensing it in March would have overstated Q1 opex by 4,200.

Net March P&L impact is **14,395.55**, not the 27,395.55 of invoice face value.

## Two things to note

**Approval threshold.** Every entry is under the 10,000 limit, so I filed no approval requests. But I'd rather you hear this from me than find it: Delmar was booked as 9,600 + a separate 800 amortization. I treated these as two distinct accounting events, not a split to dodge the threshold (which policy 1 bans). If you read the threshold as applying to the 10,400 combined, say the word and I'll route both for approval.

**I did *not* mark AP cutoff review complete** — only `in_progress`. This task covered the five named bills. A real cutoff review still needs testing for March services received but not yet invoiced (policy 5 accrual to 2100) and early-April invoices with March service periods. That's unfinished work, and closing the item would misrepresent it.

Controls tied out: AP March activity of 27,395.55 equals exactly these five bills, confirming all other March bills were paid in-month. I verified no March bank payments to any of the five, consistent with Net 30. No exceptions flagged — all five were fully supported.
